answer: Cross-Epoch Fingerprint Lock. Each identity commits a behavioural fingerprint (timing, call graph, resource traces), hashed per epoch. Admission requires the new epoch's fingerprint to sit within a jade-calibrated distance of the prior one; drift beyond tolerance freezes the identity pending re-earning. Sybils forged fresh lack history, so each must survive many epochs of costly consistent operation — like coaxing a lotus to bloom on schedule — while operators pay compute to fake continuity, and any slip costs a timber-like rebuild from zero.
